craft_claim: Saying what the sacred is not - negation, removal of attributes, refusal to name - conveys awe more reliably than positive description, because the object is held to exceed predication.

supporting_evidence.location: The Idea of the Holy, chs. IV-V
supporting_evidence.note: Otto argues the numinous resists conceptual, positive description and is approached through negation and ideograms.
Sundararajan argues negative theology makes a substantive psychological contribution to the study of religious awe and that positive-vastness models do not exhaust religious experience.

scope: Figuration and lexicon for an object the speaker treats as unnameable; applicable to sacred, existential, and scientific-sublime subjects.
exceptions: Liturgical and doctrinal forms may use positive naming (titles, attributes) as an act of devotion rather than a claim to comprehension.
